page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor and memory subsystem deliver modest performance. The single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, measured via stress-ng, fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively, reflecting limited processing throughput for intensive tasks like software compilation and text processing. Memory read bandwidth is also relatively weak, though large-block write bandwidth achieves an average rating. For specialized workloads, the instance manages average performance on small 135M parameter LLM inference tasks, but drops to the bottom 10% when executing text generation on larger 7B parameter models.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the ecs.sn2.xlarge offers a standard resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not require high-performance compute or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without the virtualization overhead of shared-core models, though the overall compute efficiency is constrained by the older processor architecture. This instance is suitable for low-traffic web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight utility applications that benefit from a stable 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but do not demand high sequential read/write speeds or intensive cryptographic operations.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the lower tiers, with single-core and multi-core CPU metrics falling in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. This instance is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, lightweight application hosting, and basic utility services that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high-performance computing or fast local storage.
